cta.title: Pipe Anything Into DuckDB
cta.description: Install the `Shellfs` extension to treat shell pipelines as readable / writable filenames — read_csv 'seq 1 100 | grep 2 |' just works.

quickStart.title: Read CSV from a shell command
quickStart.description: The printf command emits a header and two rows. A trailing pipe tells Shellfs to read the command’s standard output.
quickStart.note: Shellfs executes the command in the DuckDB process’s environment. Only use commands you intend to run, and do not build shell strings from untrusted row values.
quickStart.requirements: Use a supported native build with a Unix shell and `printf` available.

introduction.title: Use a command’s output as a SQL data source
paragraphs: Shellfs connects DuckDB’s file readers and writers to Unix processes. A command can produce the bytes that a reader consumes, or receive the output written by DuckDB.

Use it with an existing command-line tool for fetching, decompressing, or transforming data. The pipe carries bytes, so its format still needs to match the DuckDB reader or writer. Commands run on the machine hosting DuckDB, which makes this a native-client workflow.
